current-grading-unicode-15-1-repr.reason: Adopt for #233, part of #156, porting bench/tools/current_grading.py and packet_selection.py to bench-tools current-grading. Diagnostics keep the Python program name, so saved output stays identical. Records an intended difference from older interpreters, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration. Old behavior: current_grading.py quoted a source key through the running interpreter's repr, so it escaped characters that interpreter's Unicode database lacked: Python 3.12 spells U+2FFC as \u2ffc, which baseline_defect records. New behavior: bench-tools current-grading quotes through pytext::repr, which escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0). Rationale: a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: a quoted run, arm, target or path changes when it holds a character assigned after the former interpreter's Unicode version. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is 5,812 code points, those added in Unicode 15.1 and 16.0; Python 3.13 (Unicode 15.1) differs on 5,185 and Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) on 11,130. No tracked run, arm or target name holds one. This case pins U+2FFC, added in Unicode 15.1. Resolving issue: #233.

current-grading-comment-equivalent-and-r.reason: Revised for #256 after its local independent review, which found that the v2 rule left a comment equivalent to two claims with the earlier diagnostic, which names no claim, although #256 requires the refusal to name the comment and the claims. The case's bytes are unchanged; only this record's reason changes, because its v2 reason said that comment still gets the earlier message. Adopt for #256, part of #156. Authority: the owner's ruling on #230 question 2 (2026-10-19, https://github.com/kamui/code-review-bench/issues/230#issuecomment-6274330595), which enforces the owner's 2026-10-11 ruling recorded in docs/research/regrade-rulings-2026-10-13/filing/README.md: a comment linked to two or more claims is linked to none of them as equivalent. A deliberate new rule, not a port. Old behavior: current_grading.py and bench-tools current-grading check refused only a comment equivalent to two claims ('conflicting canonical duplicate group'), so a record with a comment equivalent to one claim and related to another checked as valid, exit 0, which baseline_defect records through the harness driver. New behavior: bench_tools::current_grading::validate_documents refuses that record, so bench-tools current-grading check, status and fingerprints exit 1, printing the comment's review path and item id and the claims that link it in claim order. A comment equivalent to two claims now gets the same diagnostic, as current-grading-comment-equivalent-to-two-claims records. Rationale: the 2026-10-11 ruling was enforced by hand and by test_regrade_filing.py for one filing; the owner ruled to make it a validator rule after #233. Authority: the owner's ruling on #230 question 2 (2026-10-19, https://github.com/kamui/code-review-bench/issues/230#issuecomment-6274330595), which enforces the owner's 2026-10-11 ruling: a comment linked to two or more claims is linked to none of them as equivalent; #256 requires the refusal to name the comment and the claims. Changes a diagnostic on purpose. Old behavior: current_grading.py and bench-tools current-grading check refused a comment equivalent to two claims with "<comment>: conflicting canonical duplicate group", exit 1, naming the review path and item id only, which baseline_defect records through the harness driver. New behavior: bench-tools current-grading check, status and fingerprints refuse it with the #256 diagnostic, exit 1, naming the comment and the claims that link it in claim order; the earlier check is removed because the #256 rule covers every comment it refused (a claim cannot link one comment twice). Rationale: one rule and one message for every comment linked to two or more claims with an equivalent link, and the claims named so the filer can see which links to narrow. Compatibility impact: refusal and exit code are unchanged; only the stdout line differs. No caller parses it. The current record has no comment equivalent to two claims (0 of the 174 comments linked to two or more claims carry an equivalent link on 2026-10-19), so it still checks as valid. A record with such a comment and another fault later in claim order is now reported by its other fault first, because the rule runs after every claim is read. grade.py map, regrade.py and the explorer export keep the old message through the retained current_grading.py until #156 slices 4, 8 and 10 move them. Resolving issue: #256. Expected bytes are the Rust output; baseline_defect is the retained Python's under Python 3.14.7 through the harness driver.

current-grading-help-before-invalid-shor.reason: Adopt for #268, part of #156, whose delivery plan ports each Python command line to bench-tools with argparse's arguments and exit codes. bench-tools current-grading: --help before -h=1 prints the help and exits 0, because argparse acts on --help as soon as it reads it. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: bench/tools/current_grading.py printed argparse's help and exited 0, where bench-tools refused the later -h=1 with exit 2. New behavior: bench-tools current-grading prints clap's help and exits 0; main.rs refuses -h, or a run of h's, with an attached = or - argument only when it is the first help before --, for every subcommand. Rationale: argparse acts on the first help it reads, so an earlier --help, or a unique prefix of it such as --hel, wins over a later -h=1. Compatibility impact: the exit code now matches Python's; only the help wording differs, as for every bench-tools help. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #268.
